mergedParams.userDescription: Kinetic zoom punch elastic stretch transition effects between videos

output.title: Kinetic Zoom Punch Elastic Stretch Video Transitions

prompts.prompt: Create a dynamic elastic zoom punch transition preset that creates an explosive zoom-in effect on the outgoing video, stretching and distorting it elastically before snapping to the incoming video with a reverse zoom-out punch. The outgoing video should scale up dramatically (to 150-200%) with elastic easing while simultaneously applying a radial blur effect that intensifies at the peak of the zoom. During the 0.8-second overlap period, the incoming video starts at 50% scale and punches forward to 110% before settling to 100% with a spring-like bounce. Add subtle camera shake effects (using transform translate) during the transition peak to enhance the kinetic energy. The transition should feel like the viewer is being pulled through a wormhole between scenes.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout container with 'relative w-full h-full overflow-hidden' and duration calculated as video1.duration + video2.duration - 0.8s overlap. Two VideoAtom components positioned with 'absolute inset-0'. Outgoing video uses generic transform effect with AnimationRange scaling from 1 to 2 with elastic easing (cubic-bezier(0.68, -0.55, 0.265, 1.55)) and filter effect for radial blur (0px to 20px). Incoming video starts at startFrom: video1.duration - 0.8, uses transform effect scaling from 0.5 to 1.1 to 1.0 with spring easing. Add shake effect using transform translate with random values (-10px to 10px) applied rapidly during the 0.3s-0.5s range of the transition. Use provider mode effects with targetIds for each video. Z-index: incoming video at z-10, outgoing at z-0.

prompts.prompt: Design a kinetic stretch warp transition that horizontally stretches the outgoing video like it's being pulled through a dimensional portal, while the incoming video emerges from the center with a vertical stretch that normalizes. The outgoing video should stretch horizontally to 300% width while maintaining height, creating a smeared motion blur effect. Simultaneously, apply a perspective transform that makes it appear to recede into the distance. The incoming video starts as a thin vertical line (10% width, 200% height) and expands outward with elastic momentum. Include pulsing opacity flickers during the transition to simulate dimensional instability. The 0.6-second overlap should feel like reality is being torn and reformed.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full overflow-hidden bg-black' and duration = video1.duration + video2.duration - 0.6s. Outgoing VideoAtom with transform effect: scaleX animates 1 to 3, perspective transforms from 0 to 1000px with rotateY from 0 to -45deg. Apply motion blur filter (0 to 30px horizontal). Incoming VideoAtom starts at video1.duration - 0.6, transform effect: scaleX from 0.1 to 1 with overshoot, scaleY from 2 to 1. Opacity effects with rapid keyframes (1, 0.7, 1, 0.8, 1) over 0.2s intervals during transition. Both videos use 'absolute inset-0 object-cover'. Provider mode with distinct targetIds. Consider adding CSS will-change: transform for performance.

prompts.prompt: Build a zoom vortex transition where both videos spiral into each other with rotating zoom effects, creating a whirlpool-like visual. The outgoing video zooms out while rotating clockwise (360 degrees), simultaneously decreasing opacity in a pulsing pattern. The incoming video emerges from the center, rotating counter-clockwise (720 degrees) while scaling up from 0% to 100% with elastic bounce-back. Add chromatic aberration effects by splitting RGB channels slightly during the peak rotation. The 1-second overlap should include rapid zoom pulses (scale oscillating between 90-110%) to enhance the kinetic energy. Position both videos to rotate around a shared center point.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout container 'relative w-full h-full overflow-hidden bg-gradient-radial from-black to-transparent'. Duration = video1.duration + video2.duration - 1.0s. Outgoing VideoAtom with transform-origin: center, transform effect: scale from 1 to 0.3, rotate from 0 to 360deg over 1s with ease-in-out. Opacity pulses using AnimationRange with values [1, 0.8, 1, 0.6, 0.3, 0]. Incoming VideoAtom (startFrom: video1.duration - 1.0) with transform: scale from 0 to 1.1 to 1, rotate from -720deg to 0 with elastic easing. Add filter effects for RGB channel splitting using drop-shadow with offset values. Z-index layering: incoming z-20, outgoing z-10. Use GPU-accelerated transforms with transform3d.

prompts.prompt: Create a kinetic shatter zoom transition where the outgoing video appears to shatter into fragments that zoom past the camera while the incoming video assembles from scattered pieces zooming in. Simulate the shatter effect by using multiple overlay divs with clip-path polygons that animate outward with different velocities and rotation speeds. The incoming video uses inverse clip-paths that converge from the edges. During the 0.7-second overlap, add explosive shake effects and rapid zoom pulses. Include motion blur that follows the direction of each fragment's movement. The transition should feel like breaking through glass between dimensions.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full overflow-hidden'. Create fragment overlays using additional BaseLayout divs with clip-path: polygon() values creating triangular/rectangular shards. Outgoing video with base transform scaling to 1.5, then fragment overlays animate with transform: translate and rotate with different values per shard (translate up to 200% in various directions). Incoming video (startFrom: video1.duration - 0.7) starts with scale: 0.1 and fragments use clip-path animations from scattered to assembled. Motion blur using filter: blur() with directional values. Shake effect using rapid translate transforms (-20px to 20px) at 60fps intervals. Provider mode effects targeting video atoms and overlay elements.

prompts.prompt: Design an elastic slingshot zoom transition that pulls the outgoing video back like a rubber band before launching it forward and replacing it with the incoming video that snaps into place. The outgoing video first scales down to 70% with tension, then rapidly scales up to 250% while rotating slightly (15 degrees) and applying motion blur. The incoming video starts extremely small (5%) and positioned off-center, then slingshots into place with overshoot animation (scaling to 120% before settling to 100%). Add vibration effects during the snap moment using rapid position changes. The 0.5-second overlap should include speed lines effect using gradient overlays.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout 'relative w-full h-full overflow-hidden' with calculated duration. Outgoing VideoAtom animates with transform keyframes: scale 1 → 0.7 (0-0.2s) → 2.5 (0.2-0.5s), rotate 0 → -15deg → 0. Motion blur filter: 0 → 40px following movement direction. Incoming VideoAtom (startFrom: video1.duration - 0.5) positioned initially at 'absolute top-1/4 left-1/4' with scale: 0.05, animates to 'inset-0' with scale 0.05 → 1.2 → 1.0 using spring physics easing. Vibration via transform: translate with rapid random values. Speed lines using ::before/::after pseudo-elements with linear gradients animated across screen.

prompts.prompt: Build a quantum zoom tunnel transition where both videos create a tunnel effect with recursive zoom layers, simulating traveling through a time vortex. The outgoing video duplicates into multiple layers, each scaling and fading at different rates to create depth. The incoming video emerges from the tunnel center with inverse scaling layers. Apply swirling distortion effects using CSS transforms with perspective and rotateZ. During the 0.9-second overlap, add stroboscopic opacity flashes and color channel shifts. The videos should appear to stretch infinitely into a vanishing point before snapping to the new scene.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with perspective: 1000px and transform-style: preserve-3d. Create 5 duplicate layers of outgoing video using multiple VideoAtom components with staggered z-index (0, -100, -200, -300, -400) and scaling (1, 0.8, 0.6, 0.4, 0.2). Each layer has different opacity fade timing. Transform animations include translateZ for depth and rotateZ for spiral effect. Incoming video layers (startFrom: video1.duration - 0.9) scale from 0 to 1 with inverse z-positioning. Strobe effect using opacity AnimationRange with rapid toggles (0.05s intervals). Color shifts using filter: hue-rotate() animated from 0 to 180deg. GPU optimization with will-change: transform, opacity.

prompts.prompt: Create a kinetic accordion zoom transition that compresses the outgoing video horizontally into vertical strips that zoom away while the incoming video expands from compressed strips zooming in. The outgoing video splits into 8 vertical segments using clip-path, each animating with different zoom speeds and slight rotation for a venetian blind effect. The incoming video uses complementary strip animations that unfold from the center. Add elastic bounce effects when strips reach their destinations. Include a brief moment where both videos create a striped pattern during the 0.6-second overlap. Apply alternating blur effects to enhance the depth perception.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout container with 'relative w-full h-full overflow-hidden'. Outgoing video with 8 clip-path rectangles (using calc() for dynamic widths), each animating scaleX from 1 to 0.1 and translateZ for depth, with staggered delays (0.05s apart). Rotation alternates between -5deg and 5deg per strip. Incoming VideoAtom (startFrom: video1.duration - 0.6) with inverse clip-paths animating scaleX from 0.1 to 1 with elastic easing. Blur effects alternate: odd strips blur(0 to 3px), even strips stay sharp. Z-index layering for proper strip ordering. Transform-origin set to center for each strip. Add box-shadow for depth during compression.

prompts.prompt: Design a hyperzoom glitch transition that rapidly zooms between macro and micro scales while introducing digital glitch artifacts. The outgoing video experiences exponential zoom-in (to 1000% scale) with RGB channel separation and datamosh-style displacement. The incoming video starts at extreme zoom (0.1% scale) and exponentially grows while glitching through multiple resolution states. During the 0.4-second overlap, add scan lines, pixel sorting effects, and random frame holds that create a stuttering zoom effect. Include brief moments where both videos become pixelated or posterized. The transition should feel like diving through digital space at light speed.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full overflow-hidden bg-black'. Outgoing VideoAtom with transform: scale animating exponentially from 1 to 10 using custom cubic-bezier. RGB split using three filter: drop-shadow() with red, green, blue offsets. Glitch displacement using transform: skew() with random values. Incoming VideoAtom (startFrom: video1.duration - 0.4) scales from 0.001 to 1 with stuttering keyframes (hold positions at 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7). Scan lines via ::after pseudo-element with repeating linear gradient. Pixelation using filter: contrast() and brightness() spikes. Random transform: translate() jumps for frame holds. Mix-blend-mode: screen during overlap peak.

prompts.prompt: Build a spiral drill zoom transition where videos rotate and zoom as if drilling through layers of reality. The outgoing video spins clockwise while zooming in, creating a drill bit effect with increasing rotation speed (accelerating from 0 to 1080 degrees). Apply a twist distortion using multiple transform points along the spiral path. The incoming video counter-rotates (1440 degrees) while emerging from the center point, starting as a tiny dot and expanding with decreasing rotation speed. Add metallic shine effects during rotation peaks and particle debris effects at the drill point. The 0.8-second overlap should include oscillating scale pulses that simulate drilling resistance.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with radial gradient background and transform-style: preserve-3d. Outgoing VideoAtom with transform-origin: center, animating rotate from 0 to 1080deg with ease-in acceleration, scale from 1 to 3. Path animation using offset-path for spiral movement. Twist effect using skew transforms at multiple keyframes. Incoming VideoAtom (startFrom: video1.duration - 0.8) with rotate from -1440deg to 0 with ease-out, scale from 0.01 to 1. Metallic shine using animated linear-gradient overlay. Scale pulses using AnimationRange with oscillating values (0.9, 1.1, 0.95, 1.05). Particle effects using absolutely positioned divs with scatter animations. Blur increases with rotation speed using calculated filter values.

prompts.prompt: Create a rubber band snap zoom transition that stretches videos like elastic material before snapping into the next scene. The outgoing video stretches diagonally (scale X to 200%, Y to 50%) while twisting with a rubber-like deformation, then snaps away with intense acceleration. The incoming video starts compressed (scale X to 50%, Y to 200%) and snaps into place with multiple bounce oscillations. Add wobble effects using alternating skew transforms during the elastic deformation. Include motion trails using duplicated semi-transparent layers that follow the main video with slight delays. The 0.7-second overlap features maximum stretch tension with visible stress lines rendered as animated gradients.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout 'relative w-full h-full overflow-hidden'. Outgoing VideoAtom with transform animations: scaleX 1 → 2 → 0, scaleY 1 → 0.5 → 3, skewX alternating -20deg to 20deg, using elastic easing with tension parameters. Motion trails using 3 duplicate video layers at opacity 0.3, 0.2, 0.1 with 0.05s delay each. Incoming VideoAtom (startFrom: video1.duration - 0.7) with inverse scaling and spring physics (damping: 0.3, stiffness: 200). Wobble via skew animations with sine wave patterns. Stress lines using ::before with animated linear gradients (45deg angle) at 50% opacity during peak stretch. Transform-origin shifts during animation for realistic deformation. GPU accelerated with transform3d and will-change.
